insights.observation: Name-to-Value mapping has controlled mutation; insertion first attempts the requested name, then retries suffix candidates against the actual occupied map. Reinsertion can rename while retaining the associated Value.
insights.ink_application: Use occupied ambient parameter sets for generated proof names, retaining the requested stem when free and retrying on collisions. Numeric counters alone do not establish freshness.

insights.observation: The bounded-name path truncates and rechecks collisions; global names use target-dependent dot policy because NVPTX identifier syntax differs.
insights.ink_application: Keep proof/source identifiers distinct from target symbol formatting. Do not import LLVM truncation or naming syntax as proof equality or semantic identity.

insights.observation: Removing a table entry leaves the ValueName attached; destruction checks table emptiness only in debug builds.
insights.ink_application: A name registry does not establish ownership, lifetime, admission or immutable checked-state authority. Continue sealed CheckedModule and independent proof replay.

limits: This is a source audit of these two files, not the whole Value implementation or optimizer.
No LLVM code was transplanted; Ink already uses named proof terms and must preserve their lexical references.
Fresh-name changes are untrusted authoring improvements, not a weakening of the kernel.
